scale.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml): "1000000000: biljun[ u >>];" names 10^9, the short scale.

group_mark.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, MSA Specification for Maltese locale (2009), 4.3 Numeric formatting: "The thousands separator is the COMMA (,)"; CLDR 49.0.0 (unicode-org/cldr-json), cldr-numbers-full/main/mt/numbers.json, symbols-numberSystem-latn: "group": ",".

decimal_mark.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, MSA Specification for Maltese locale (2009), 4.3 Numeric formatting: "The decimal separator is the FULL STOP (.)"; CLDR 49.0.0 (unicode-org/cldr-json), cldr-numbers-full/main/mt/numbers.json, symbols-numberSystem-latn: "decimal": ".".

space_groups.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, MSA Specification for Maltese locale (2009), 4.3 Numeric formatting: "Example: 12,345.67": a comma, not a space, groups the digits.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "2000000: <%spellout-cardinal-masculine< miljuni[ u >>];": the plural follows a count. en.wiktionary, "eluf": "a vague number far beyond 1000": the plural alone names no number.

scale_noun_agrees.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, Ewro, Appendiċi B (pages/knim-ewro.decoded.txt): "tlettax-il miljun ewro" (€13,000,000): the singular scale word takes a count above one.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: [>> u ]għoxrin;": the unit goes before the ten, so no ten takes a unit after it.

tens_order.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: [>> u ]għoxrin;"; Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, Ewro, Appendiċi B (pages/knim-ewro.decoded.txt): "tnejn u ħamsin ewro" (EUR 52).

joiner_unit_ten.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: [>> u ]għoxrin;"; Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, Ewro, Appendiċi B (pages/knim-ewro.decoded.txt): "ħamsa u għoxrin ċenteżmu" (25ċ).

unit_ten_one_word.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, Ewro, Appendiċi B (pages/knim-ewro.decoded.txt): "ħamsa u għoxrin ċenteżmu": the unit, "u" and the ten are three written words.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "100: mija[ u >>];"; Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, Ewro, Appendiċi B (pages/knim-ewro.decoded.txt): "mija u tletin elf ewro".

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: elf[ u >>];", "1000000: miljun[ u >>];".

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: elf[ u >>];" puts "u" before every group after the thousands, a round hundred too.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "1000: elf[ u >>];", "2000: elfejn[ u >>];".

comma_between_classes.source: structural, no external source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering writes "u" between two classes and no comma, and no saved page shows a comma there.

letter_folds.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-cardinal-feminine: "4: erbaʼ;" writes the apostrophe of "erba'" with U+02BC, a letter to the tokenizer, where Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, Ewro, Appendiċi B (pages/knim-ewro.decoded.txt) writes "'" ("ta' l-ewro"). The fold drops U+02BC, so both spellings read alike.

word_chars.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, MSA Specification for Maltese locale (2009), 4.3 Numeric formatting: "il-ħuta ħuta, il-", "ix-xemx xemx, ix-": the article is written joined to its word by a hyphen, and the word sorts without it. The hyphen is part of the word, so the article comes off as a clitic.

clitic_min_rest.source: structural, no external source: the shortest Maltese number word after an article has two letters or more.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-ordinal: "10: għaxar;", "11: =%spellout-numbering=;": an ordinal is one word up to the tenth, and the cardinal above it, so no ordinal has several ordinal words.

joiner.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "20: [>> u ]għoxrin;", "100: mija[ u >>];".

decimal_marker.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "x.x: << punt >>;".

minus.source: CLDR RBNF mt (unicode-org/cldr release-49, common/rbnf/mt.xml), %spellout-numbering: "-x: minus >>;".

minus_idioms.source: structural, no external source: no saved page shows an idiom where "minus" stands before a number and is no sign.

article_one.source: structural, no external source: Maltese has a definite article only (en.wiktionary, "il-": "the"); the numeral "wieħed" counts one.

of.source: structural, no external source: no Maltese word stands between a plural noun and a scale word in this lexicon.

fraction_of.source: structural, no external source: this lexicon reads no word between a fraction and a collective.

denominator_particle.source: structural, no external source: Maltese puts no particle after a denominator.

class_noun.source: structural, no external source: this lexicon has no collective, so no noun names a class after one.

half_unit.source: structural, no external source: this lexicon lists no unit that a half before it halves.

abbreviation.source: structural, no external source: no Maltese number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: Kunsill Nazzjonali tal-Ilsien Malti, MSA Specification for Maltese locale (2009), 4.3 Numeric formatting: "The decimal separator is the FULL STOP (.)".

clitic_prefix.source: en.wiktionary, "il-": "the article will have the according forms", "iċ-", "id-", "in-", "ir-", "is-", "it-", "ix-", "iz-", "iż-"; en.wiktionary, "fil-", "tal-", "bil-", "għall-", "mal-", "mill-": the article joined to a preposition.
